## About
The Game Poker Club is a poker room tucked off SW Barbur Blvd in Portland. You pay a door and membership fee for the day, and the house takes no rake from the pots. Our dealers work for tips.
We get regulars, folks driving up from the Salem area, and visitors passing through town. One reviewer who stopped in from California said the dealers were friendly, professional and knowledgeable.
If you have never played in a card room before, you are welcome here. One reviewer told us it was their first poker room and that both the staff and the players made them feel at home. We're rated 4.4 from 135 Google reviews.

## Services
- $1/$2 cash game: One visitor said our $1/$2 cash game had great action.
- Mixed games: We also run a variety of mixed games.
- Day membership: Pay the door and membership fee once for the day. No rake is taken from the pots. ($20)

## FAQ
Q: How do you make money without a rake?
A: You pay a $20 door and membership fee for the day, and the house takes no rake from the pots.

Q: I can't find you. Where are you?
A: We're on SW Barbur Blvd in Portland, set back in a little alley, so keep an eye out as you pull in. Give us a call if you get turned around.

## What customers say
- "The Game Poker Club was the first poker room I'd ever set foot in, and I'll be honest — I was nervous it would be intimidating and super serious. It was the complete opposite. From the moment I walked in, both the staff and the players made me feel welcome, and the community turned out to be the best part.
There's such a good atmosphere here. Some of the regulars bring in free baked goodies that anyone's welcome to grab, and if that's not your thing, the owner happens to be a fantastic chef with plenty of meal options on hand. You will not go hungry. There's even a masseuse you can get worked on while you play — which, after a long session, hits different.
The people are what make it, though. Branko, the manager who runs the place, is a genuinely nice and fair guy. Brantifa is endlessly cheerful and enthusiastic. Rachel is kind and super helpful if you're new, but watch out — she'll have you crying laughing with her sarcasm. Oh, and a friendly warning: keep an eye on Dylan, because he will happily shark you for every chip you've got. You've been warned.
If you've never played in a poker room before and you're worried it'll be cold or cutthroat, this is the place to start. Fun atmosphere, great food, and a community that actually makes you feel like you belong.
— Mr. Wayne" (Bruce, 5/5)
- "First time in Portland, and I heard about this place. I was unsure what to expect, and was pleasantly surprised at the entire experience.  When you walk in you pay a $20 buy-in fee to the game and there is no rake all night. Never seen this system before where the dealers work only for tips and the house gets no rake. There are a total of 7 tables.  I was there on a Friday night and three of the tables were running pretty full. The dealers are friendly. The servers are very helpful, and overall a very good experience in Portland.  Finding it was a little bit tough because it’s in a little alley but overall I would highly recommend this Poker Room in Portland." (deepu budhrani, 5/5)
- "One of the best places to play in Oregon. $500 max on the 1/2 NL is good and being a first 5 players of the day and paying no door fee is nice. They run a nice variety of mixed games although I wish there was a larger fixed limit O8 game that ran there so I didn’t have to drive all the way to LaCenter. Other than that the staff are great and the action every time I’ve been is solid. If you live in the Salem area and want to play cash come to the game and save an hour round trip on your driving." (Jackson Christian, 5/5)
- "Excellent card room! Stopped in on a visit from California and was very impressed. Great action on a $1/$2 cash game of NLH without getting too crazy. Dealers were friendly, professional, and knowledgeable. Love the system of a $20 door/membership fee for the day and no house rake. Will definitely return next time I’m in Portland." (Cristian Amaral, 5/5)
